adjudication_records.issue_text: `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == raw_html`, bypassing the sanitize/cook pipeline and `Plugin::Filter`, so third-party feed HTML rendered via `raw post.cooked` becomes stored XSS

adjudication.rationale:
The diff explicitly adds a new `cook_method` enum and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`) and also bypasses `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` because it returns before that call.

The new feed/embed import paths set `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` when creating posts (`TopicEmbed.import` via `PostCreator`). For RSS polling, the imported `content` comes from `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` and is used as HTML (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`), with no sanitization shown in the diff before it is stored and later rendered. The embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any unsafe HTML in the feed content would be output verbatim.

Even if `ruby-readability` applies some tag/attribute restrictions in `import_remote`, the RSS path (`PollFeed`) does not, so the bypass is a verifiable stored XSS risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `TopicEmbed` 'Imported from' footer interpolates the feed-supplied `url` into an anchor tag unescaped, allowing HTML/attribute injection past the weak `^https?://` check

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import` appends an “Imported from” footer as raw HTML: `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")`. The only validation on `url` is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes/angle brackets. A feed-supplied URL like `http://x.com' onclick='alert(1)` would break out of the single-quoted `href` attribute and inject arbitrary attributes/HTML. This HTML is then stored as the post `raw` with `cook_method: :raw_html` (skipping the cooking/sanitization pipeline) and rendered via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `embed/best.html.erb`, making the injection exploitable (XSS).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)` in `Jobs::PollFeed` re-decodes entities the feed deliberately escaped, turning `<script>` back into live markup before storage

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed`, the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then passes that into `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for `:raw_html`, skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view then renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. As a result, a feed item that intentionally escaped markup like `<script>...</script>` will be decoded into literal `<script>...</script>` and stored/rendered as live HTML/JS, creating a verifiable XSS vector introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Already-shipped migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` was edited to add `force: true`, silently dropping the existing `top_topics` table and its data on any migration replay

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` causes the table to be dropped if it already exists before being created (typically via `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS`), which would remove any existing `top_topics` data if this migration is ever replayed (e.g., migrate:reset / rebuild / rerun in an environment where the table exists). This is a concrete behavior change introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses `open(url).read` with no scheme allowlist, redirect restriction, timeout, or response-size cap, permitting SSRF via redirects to internal addresses and worker hangs on large/slow responses

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` directly (via `open-uri`) with no options for `open_timeout`, `read_timeout`, redirect policy, or maximum response size, and it does not validate/allowlist the URL scheme. This is verifiable in the diff: `import_remote` accepts arbitrary `url` and passes it to `open(url).read` unchanged. While `TopicRetriever` checks the initial host against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, `open-uri` can follow redirects to other hosts by default, so an allowed-host URL that redirects can still cause SSRF to internal addresses. Separately, because there are no timeouts/size caps, the job/task can hang or consume large memory on slow/large responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `TopicRetriever` uses `$redis.setnx` followed by a separate `$redis.expire`, which is non-atomic; a failure between calls leaves the throttle key without a TTL, blocking that URL forever

adjudication.rationale:
In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the code implements throttling as:

- `if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")`
- then `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`

These are two separate Redis commands. If the process crashes or loses connectivity after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` is executed, the key will be created without a TTL and will persist indefinitely. Since subsequent calls will see `setnx` fail, `retrieved_recently?` will keep returning true, effectively blocking retrieval for that embed_url forever. This is a real correctness issue introduced by the diff (it adds the entire TopicRetriever implementation).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `TopicEmbed` does a check-then-act (`where(embed_url:).first` then `create!`) that races under concurrent importers and raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` against the unique index

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, it does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url, ...)`. The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` adds a unique index on `:embed_url`. Under concurrent callers importing the same URL, both can observe `embed.blank?` and both attempt `create!`, causing one to raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. The surrounding `Topic.transaction` does not prevent this race because it doesn’t lock the `topic_embeds` row (it doesn’t exist yet) or otherwise serialize by `embed_url`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs, so `//cdn.example.com/img.png` is rewritten into a broken absolute path

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, both link and image rewriting use `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')` (and similarly for `src`). This condition is true for protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png`. The rewrite then does `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`, which would turn `//cdn.example.com/img.png` into something like `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/img.png`, breaking the intended external CDN URL. This is a concrete, verifiable correctness bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` synchronously runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`, re-downloading the entire feed on every embed cache miss; the per-`embed_url` throttle allows unlimited full-feed fetches (amplification vector)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (not enqueued), which in turn calls `poll_feed` and performs `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`, downloading/parsing the entire feed and iterating all items. The only rate limiting in `TopicRetriever` is `retrieved_recently?`, keyed by the full `@embed_url` (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so a caller can vary `embed_url` (e.g., different paths/querystrings on the allowed host) to bypass the per-URL throttle and trigger repeated full-feed fetches on embed cache misses. This is a concrete performance/DoS amplification vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `t.string :embed_url` is varchar(255), too short for real article URLs with tracking params, causing Postgres 'value too long' insert failures with no fallback

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `topic_embeds` table with `t.string :embed_url, null: false` (no `limit:` specified), which in Rails maps to `varchar(255)` by default. The code stores arbitrary external article URLs (`TopicEmbed.import(user, url, ...)` and `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, url, ...)`) without truncation or fallback, and also adds a unique index on `embed_url`. If an embed/article URL exceeds 255 characters (common with long paths or tracking/query params), Postgres will raise a “value too long” error on insert/update. This is a concrete schema/code mismatch introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: On the update path `embed.post` can be `nil` for a deleted post (no dependent handling/cleanup), so `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises NoMethodError

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally does `PostRevisor.new(post)` when `content_sha1` changes. Even though `topic_embeds.post_id` is `null: false`, the associated `Post` can still be missing (e.g., the post was deleted, or the DB contains a dangling `post_id` since no FK/dependent cleanup is shown in the diff). In that case `embed.post` returns `nil` and `PostRevisor.new(nil)` will later dereference `@post` and raise a `NoMethodError`. There is no guard for `post.blank?` and no cleanup logic in this diff to prevent orphaned `topic_embeds`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The Disqus import replacement `TopicEmbed.import_remote` drops the `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` argument, stamping every imported topic with the import date and losing historical ordering

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the old code created the first post/topic with `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`. The new replacement calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which in app/models/topic_embed.rb ultimately calls `PostCreator.new(..., title: title, raw: ..., skip_validations: true, cook_method: ...)` without any `created_at`. PostCreator (lib/post_creator.rb) only sets `post.created_at` when `@opts[:created_at]` is present, so imported topics/posts will default to the current time, losing historical timestamps/ordering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `--category`/`-c` option was removed from the Disqus thor task with no deprecation, breaking existing invocations and silently redirecting imports to the default category

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` the `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` line is removed, along with all logic that looked up `category_id` and passed `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. The task now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which does not supply any category information. This is a backwards-incompatible CLI change: existing invocations using `--category`/`-c` will fail due to an unknown option, and even if users stop passing it, imports will no longer be placed into the specified category (they'll fall back to whatever default/category behavior is).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `embed_controller_spec` stubs `TopicRetriever.new`/`retrieve` while the controller now calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`; there is no test that the job is enqueued with the right `embed_url`/`user_id` and no test for `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`

adjudication.rationale: In the new `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` is found it does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and never instantiates `TopicRetriever`. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` includes a test (`"tells the topic retriever to work..."`) that stubs/expects `TopicRetriever.new` and `retriever.retrieve`. That expectation is inconsistent with the controller code in the diff and would fail; the spec should instead assert the job enqueue (and/or add specs for `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The embed loading page reloads every 30s indefinitely with no attempt cap while `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` allows caching, causing endless iframe reloads when retrieval permanently fails

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` is found it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and `render 'loading'`, but still calls `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` for that response. The `loading.html.erb` template executes `document.location.reload();` every 30 seconds with no stopping condition. If the embed retrieval never succeeds (e.g., invalid URL, network error, wrong settings), the iframe will reload indefinitely. Additionally, because `location.reload()` is called without forcing a revalidation and the response is explicitly cacheable for 1 minute, the browser can keep reusing the cached loading page, making the 30s polling ineffective and contributing to an endless loop until cache expiry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `contents << "\n<hr>..."` mutates the caller's string in place, duplicating footers on reuse/re-import and raising RuntimeError on a frozen string literal

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, title, contents)`, the line `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends to the passed-in `contents` String in place. This is a concrete side effect visible in the diff: if the caller reuses the same String object for multiple imports, the footer will be appended repeatedly and the computed `content_sha1` will change accordingly. Also, if a caller passes a frozen String (possible under `# frozen_string_literal: true` or explicit `freeze`), `<<` will raise (FrozenError/RuntimeError depending on Ruby).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `'<%= request.referer %>'` applies HTML escaping inside a JavaScript string context: `&` becomes `&` and a trailing backslash escapes the closing quote, breaking the script so no resize message is sent
`embed.js` has no null check on `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')`, so `comments.appendChild` throws and the message listener is never registered when the container is missing

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, `comments` is set via `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and is used immediately: `comments.appendChild(iframe);` with no guard. If the host page does not include an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be `null` and this line will throw a TypeError, which also prevents the subsequent `window.addEventListener('message', ...)` from being registered. This is a concrete runtime bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` were added to the Gemfile but only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` was regenerated, leaving the Rails 3 `Gemfile.lock` out of sync and breaking `bundle install --deployment` and CI

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Gemfile` updated to include `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss`, and only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` updated accordingly. However, the proposed finding asserts a separate Rails 3 `Gemfile.lock` exists and is now out of sync, but no `Gemfile.lock` (or any Rails 3 lockfile) is shown/modified in this diff. Without evidence in the diff that a Rails 3 lockfile exists and is expected to be updated, the claim that this will break `bundle install --deployment`/CI is not verifiable from the provided changes.
